holidays.name: National Sneak Some Zucchini Onto Your Neighbor's Porch Day
holidays.description: Late summer gardens produce more zucchini than anyone can eat. This day invites you to take the extra squash, tiptoe up to a neighbor's porch under cover of darkness, leave it there, and run. Ring-and-ditch rules apply, and the only thing you're stealing is a little peace and quiet from your own overflowing garden.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance created by holiday inventor Roy (the creator of No Socks Day and Hug Your Cat Day). It was timed for the peak of the zucchini harvest, when gardeners are most desperate to unload their bounty.
holidays.funFact: One zucchini plant can easily produce several pounds of squash a week at its peak, so gardeners often find themselves with more than they can use. That's why this holiday feels so necessary.

holidays.name: International Cat Day
holidays.description: A worldwide celebration of our whiskered, purring, keyboard-walking overlords. People mark the day by cuddling their cats, sharing photos, and supporting shelters and rescue groups. Donating litter, food or time is a popular way to join in.
holidays.origin: It was launched in 2002 by the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) to honor cats and promote their welfare around the world.
holidays.funFact: Cats sleep roughly 12 to 16 hours a day, so there's a good chance your cat spent much of its own holiday napping.

holidays.name: National Frozen Custard Day
holidays.description: A day for the dense, silky, extra-creamy cousin of ice cream. Frozen custard gets its rich texture from egg yolks and a slow-churning process that whips in very little air. Head to a custard stand and treat yourself to a cone or a concrete.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin, celebrated each August 8 by custard fans.
holidays.funFact: Frozen custard is said to have been first sold on Coney Island in 1919, where its smooth texture drew crowds of boardwalk visitors.
